doc.title: Don Menza and Sam Noto interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 28, 1997

title: Jokes about Rich and visiting him in the hospital
summary: Joke about Rich's phone, and Menza's last visit to Rich at UCLA with Jake Hanna.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: There’s really a little bit of a negative story on that thing, it’s a joke, but this guy calls after Buddy had passed he called Buddy’s number and gets his wife or somebody, his daughter, answers the phone. And he says, “Is Buddy Rich there please?” Big lull you know. “Well Buddy passed on.” He says, “Oh, okay, I just wanted to make sure.”
I heard the same thing about Benny Goodman too.
Well sure, that’s a whole hour program, Benny Goodman.
Right. We’ve had some stories, but you know most musicians are fairly protective of one another.
Oh, yeah, most of the time.
I really enjoyed your perspective on him because—

It’s different from what you — I mean it’s unreal. When he was in the hospital I remember going to see him. I was on my way to Europe and Chuck Findley and I and Joe Romano to see him. We had a ride to the airport so we stopped at UCLA and this was just after his operation, and his left arm was gone, his left arm was totally paralyzed. We never saw him again. He had died while we were in Europe and his left arm was paralyzed. And he’d be laying there. And every time he’d yawn, his arm would raise. There was something in the nerve system and his arm would go up and then fall. And while we were there Jake Hanna came in. And Jake went over and gave him a hug and Buddy started crying, and he was a very humble man, really. And he said, “oh, Buddy, you’re going to be all right, you play more with one hand.” And he says, “No, Jake, look © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-
at this,” and he picked up his hand and dropped it, and Jake in his quick sense of — his sharp sense of humor looked at Buddy and he says, “Now you know how we feel when you play.”
